title: Sejm inquiry into the Amber Gold collapse and the state's response under his first government
description: Amber Gold, a Gdańsk-based company that sold gold-backed investment products and owned the airline OLT Express, collapsed in 2012 during Tusk's first premiership, leaving thousands of clients with losses. A Sejm investigative committee set up in 2016 under the PiS majority and chaired by Małgorzata Wassermann (PiS) examined how state institutions handled the case. Tusk, then President of the European Council, testified before it as its last witness on 5 November 2018. The final report, adopted on 13 June 2019 by six votes to three, attributed the scheme's growth to 'weakness of the state'; according to RMF FM, Wassermann said the state under Tusk had been 'completely dysfunctional' and that he had not controlled the services under him (including the ABW). Opposition committee members Krzysztof Brejza (KO), Witold Zembaczyński (Nowoczesna) and Krzysztof Paszyk (PSL) filed dissenting opinions, Brejza saying the committee had sought to 'hunt down' Tusk and PO politicians. Tusk was not charged with any offence in connection with the case.
key_facts: Amber Gold collapsed in 2012, during Tusk's first term as Prime Minister
Sejm investigative committee created in 2016; Tusk testified on 5 November 2018
Final report adopted 13 June 2019 (6–3), critical of state institutions during his government
Opposition members filed dissenting opinions; no charges against Tusk

title: 2014 wiretapping scandal ('afera taśmowa') involving ministers of his government
description: In June 2014 the weekly Wprost published secretly recorded conversations of senior officials in Warsaw restaurants, including Interior Minister Bartłomiej Sienkiewicz and National Bank of Poland governor Marek Belka. On 18 June 2014 prosecutors and ABW officers attempted to seize the recordings at Wprost's offices, which the editor-in-chief refused, drawing criticism over press freedom. Tusk refused to dismiss the ministers, saying the government would not act 'under the dictate of criminals', and won a confidence vote on 25 June 2014 (237 to 203); a PiS motion of no confidence was rejected in July 2014. After the case files were posted online in June 2015, his successor Ewa Kopacz accepted the resignations of several ministers. Businessman Marek Falenta was later convicted (2.5 years) for organising the recordings.
key_facts: Recordings made in Warsaw restaurants between 2013 and 2014, published by Wprost from 14 June 2014
Tusk declined to dismiss ministers and won a confidence vote on 25 June 2014 (237–203)
Several ministers resigned in June 2015 under Prime Minister Ewa Kopacz
Marek Falenta sentenced in December 2016; verdict upheld on appeal

title: 'Special place in hell' remark about Brexit promoters
description: On 6 February 2019, as President of the European Council and after meeting Irish Taoiseach Leo Varadkar, Tusk said he had been wondering 'what that special place in hell looks like, for those who promoted Brexit without even a sketch of a plan how to carry it out safely', and repeated it on Twitter. The UK Leader of the House of Commons, Andrea Leadsom, called the remark 'pretty unacceptable and pretty disgraceful', and Nigel Farage replied that after Brexit the UK would be free of 'unelected, arrogant bullies like you'.
key_facts: Remark made at a Brussels press conference on 6 February 2019 and repeated on Twitter
Context: stalled ratification of the Withdrawal Agreement and the Irish backstop
Criticised by UK government and Brexit-supporting politicians

title: PiS-era commission on Russian influence ('lex Tusk') recommends he not hold security posts
description: In 2023 the PiS majority created a State Commission to investigate Russian influence in 2007–2022, signed into law by President Andrzej Duda on 29 May 2023 and widely nicknamed 'lex Tusk' because critics, including the Venice Commission, EU institutions and the US, said it could be used to bar opposition figures from office before the October 2023 election; Duda then proposed amendments removing the power to bar people from office. On 29 November 2023 the commission, chaired by Sławomir Cenckiewicz, published an interim report on cooperation between Poland's Military Counterintelligence Service (SKW) and Russia's FSB, recommending that Tusk and several of his former ministers not be entrusted with posts responsible for state security; Tusk said the case 'reeks of politics'. The same evening the new Sejm majority dismissed all commission members. A 2024 bill repealing the law was vetoed by Duda in August 2024, leaving the commission inactive.
key_facts: Law signed on 29 May 2023 and amended later in 2023 after domestic and international criticism
Interim report of 29 November 2023 recommended Tusk not hold state-security posts (no legal effect)
Sejm dismissed the commission's members on 29 November 2023
Repeal bill vetoed by President Duda in August 2024

title: Takeover and liquidation of the public media companies
description: Days after taking office, Tusk's government, through Culture Minister Bartłomiej Sienkiewicz, dismissed the management and supervisory boards of public broadcaster TVP, Polskie Radio and the PAP news agency on 20 December 2023 and took the TVP Info channel off the air, arguing the outlets had served as PiS propaganda tools. PiS politicians staged sit-ins at TVP and PAP, and President Duda vetoed the budget-related bill funding public media, citing a 'flagrant violation of the constitution'. On 27 December 2023 Sienkiewicz put the companies into liquidation, saying this would keep them operating; Tusk said the vetoed 3 billion PLN would go to children's cancer treatment and mental health care. Many independent legal experts questioned the method, some court registry decisions went against the government, and press-freedom group RSF said it understood that the government 'had to act quickly', while calling for a reform to depoliticise the broadcaster.
key_facts: Boards of TVP, Polskie Radio and PAP dismissed on 20 December 2023
Presidential veto of public-media funding on 23 December 2023
Companies put into liquidation on 27 December 2023
Legality of the method questioned by legal experts; parts rejected by courts

title: Admission that rule-of-law repair may 'not fully comply with the law' and 'revoked' countersignature
description: On 9 September 2024 Tusk announced he was 'revoking' his countersignature of a presidential decision appointing a judge whom the government regards as improperly appointed (a so-called 'neo-judge') to convene an electoral assembly of the Supreme Court's civil chamber, saying the signature had been given 'by mistake'. Constitutional law experts including former Constitutional Tribunal president Andrzej Zoll said there was no legal basis for withdrawing a countersignature, and the Supreme Court's spokesman said the move had no legal effect. The next day, at a Senate conference, Tusk said that in restoring constitutional order the government would probably take actions that some legal authorities would consider 'not fully compliant with the law', blaming the legal chaos left by PiS. PiS politicians ridiculed the remarks and Confederation announced a notification to prosecutors over the countersignature.
key_facts: Countersignature 'revoked' on 9 September 2024; legal experts said no such procedure exists
Remarks at the Senate conference 'Ways out of the constitutional crisis' on 10 September 2024
Confederation announced a notification to prosecutors; no outcome reported in the sources consulted

title: Suspension of the right to asylum at the Belarus border
description: In October 2024 Tusk announced a migration strategy including the temporary suspension of the right to claim asylum, arguing that existing rules were not designed for the deliberate 'instrumentalisation' of migration by Belarus and Russia. The enabling law was signed on 26 March 2025 and the suspension at the Belarus border took effect on 27 March 2025, with exceptions for minors, pregnant women and other vulnerable people; the Sejm has repeatedly extended it, the first time in May 2025 by 366 votes to 17. UNHCR and Poland's Commissioner for Human Rights said the measures breach international and EU law, and human rights groups said they also violate the Polish constitution and expose asylum seekers to pushbacks. In March 2025 Tusk also said Poland would no longer accept returns of asylum seekers under the EU's Dublin Regulation.
key_facts: Policy announced in October 2024; law signed 26 March 2025; suspension in force from 27 March 2025
Repeatedly extended by the Sejm, first in May 2025 (366–17)
Criticised by UNHCR, the Polish Commissioner for Human Rights and NGOs

title: Calls for recounts after the 2025 presidential run-off
description: After Karol Nawrocki (backed by PiS) narrowly defeated KO's Rafał Trzaskowski in the 1 June 2025 run-off, reports of counting errors in some polling stations led to tens of thousands of electoral complaints. On 20 June 2025 Tusk said that if the complaints showed falsification large enough to change the outcome, all votes nationwide should be recounted and the swearing-in should wait, while stressing he did not assume the election was invalid; his government does not recognise the Supreme Court chamber that validates elections because of how its judges were appointed. Nawrocki urged him to 'abandon the hysteria and not destroy Polish democracy', and outgoing President Duda accused the government of being unable to accept defeat. Partial recounts confirmed some errors, but on 1 July 2025 the Supreme Court's Extraordinary Control chamber validated the result, finding irregularities that 'did not affect the result'; Nawrocki took office on 6 August 2025.
key_facts: Nawrocki won the run-off by about 370,000 votes (50.89% to 49.11%)
Tusk's 20 June 2025 statement on a possible nationwide recount
Supreme Court chamber validated the election on 1 July 2025; the government disputes the chamber's legitimacy
Nawrocki sworn in on 6 August 2025

title: Accusations that the president and right-wing opposition serve Russian interests
description: At a Civic Coalition congress on 11 April 2026 Tusk accused President Karol Nawrocki, PiS and Confederation of forming a 'Putinist front' whose aims match Vladimir Putin's plan for Poland, calling the opposition a 'modern Targowica'. After President Nawrocki vetoed the SAFE defence-loans bill in March 2026 he said Poles were 'wondering whether this is treason, the work of lobbyists, or a lack of common sense'. On 6 September 2026, after the AfD's win in the Saxony-Anhalt state election, he wrote that 'only idiots or traitors' in Poland could rejoice at it, adding that many had gathered in Confederation and PiS. Opposition figures have long accused Tusk himself of representing foreign (German or Russian) interests; the exchanges illustrate the polarised tone of Polish politics ahead of the 2027 parliamentary election.
key_facts: 'Putinist front' speech at the KO congress, 11 April 2026
Reaction to the SAFE veto, March 2026
'Only idiots or traitors' post on X, 6 September 2026

title: Election of his close aide Maciej Berek to the Constitutional Tribunal
description: In August 2026 Tusk confirmed he wanted Maciej Berek, the government minister he called his 'right-hand man', to become a judge of the Constitutional Tribunal, whose PiS-era composition his government does not recognise as legitimate. Berek left the government and was elected by the Sejm on 4 September 2026 with 226 votes, with four coalition MPs, including Sejm Speaker Włodzimierz Czarzasty, voting against. Critics, including NGOs and some coalition MPs, said the choice broke the government's pledge to 'depoliticise' the tribunal and cited a 2024 law, never brought into force, that would have barred recent politicians from sitting on it; Tusk said Berek's role in government had been 'apolitical and nonpartisan'. As of October 2026 President Nawrocki, before whom judges must take the oath, opposed Berek's appointment, as he had refused to swear in four other judges elected by the Sejm in 2026.
key_facts: Berek elected by the Sejm on 4 September 2026 (226 votes of 437 cast)
Criticism that the nomination contradicts the pledge to depoliticise the tribunal
President Nawrocki opposes the appointment; the oath has not been reported as taken
